question: The northern part of the plains along the Bay of Bengal is referred to as the Northern Circar, while the southern part is known as the ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Coromandel Coast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Northern Circars:** The Northern Circars refer to the northern coastal plains along the eastern coast of India, specifically near the **Bay of Bengal**. These plains lie in the regions of present-day Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
 
• **The Southern Part:** The southern region of these plains along the eastern coastline is referred to as the **Coromandel Coast**. This area stretches along Tamil Nadu and parts of southern Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Geographical Significance:** The Coromandel Coast is known for its distinct geographical features, including flat coastal plains, sandy beaches, and proximity to the Eastern Ghats. It has a tropical climate and is influenced by monsoon winds.
 
• The term **Coromandel Coast** is derived from the historical references to the Chola dynasty, which ruled the region for centuries. It is important to highlight that the name has historical and cultural significance.
 
• **Economic Importance:** The Coromandel Coast is historically significant for trade and commerce. During colonial times, it was a major trading hub for spices, textiles, and other commodities.
 
• The plains along the Coromandel Coast are fertile and support agriculture, especially the cultivation of rice, pulses, and other crops. ***Hence, the southern part is correctly referred to as the Coromandel Coast.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Features of the Coromandel Coast:**

 
 
• The Coromandel Coast lies along the southeastern coastline of India, bordering the states of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is characterized by flat terrain, sandy beaches, lagoons, and low-lying regions. The coast is subject to frequent cyclones during the monsoon season due to its location near the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Coromandel Coast has a rich history as a center for maritime trade during the medieval period. It was an important region for the Chola dynasty, Pallavas, and other South Indian empires.
 
• Colonial powers like the British and the Dutch established trading posts here due to its strategic location for trade in spices, textiles, and other goods.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• The region is agriculturally productive, with crops like rice, sugarcane, and coconut being cultivated extensively.
 
• It is also important for fishing and aquaculture due to its proximity to the Bay of Bengal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Differences Between Northern Circars and Coromandel Coast:**

 
 
• The Northern Circars are located in the northern coastal regions, whereas the Coromandel Coast is in the southern coastal regions.
 
• The Coromandel Coast has a historical connection to the Chola dynasty, while the Northern Circars were more prominent during the colonial period for administrative divisions.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Conditions:**
 
 
• The Coromandel Coast experiences a tropical climate, with heavy rainfall during the northeast monsoon. The Northern Circars receive rainfall mainly from the southwest monsoon.
 
• Cyclones are common along the Coromandel Coast due to its proximity to the Bay of Bengal.
